raw: 39.1 Inoculation Theory: McGuire and Papageorgis (1961) to Present[^181][^182]
teaching_note: Psychological inoculation uses a forewarning and a refutation of a weakened misleading argument or technique before later exposure; the medical analogy does not establish immunity, a clinical effect, or protection against every future claim. Distinguish technique recognition, factual discernment, sharing intention, observed behavior, and durability. The cited contemporary reviews discuss the theory's history; they are not themselves the 1961 primary experiments [@ageint181; @ageint182].
title: Inoculation Theory: McGuire and Papageorgis (1961) to Present

teaching_note: Read ageint182 with its [2025 correction](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12391837/) and [Loughnan et al. critique](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12428163/), not as an uncontested pooled verdict. The correction expands eligibility to quasi-experiments and clarifies discernment coding, reconstruction, and equal-arm sample imputation; the authors report comparable pooled effects after removing one quasi-experiment. The critique separately challenges outcome classification, experimental-condition selection, sample estimates, and active/passive coding; that sensitivity result does not by itself resolve every objection. The paper is not described here as retracted, nor do these concerns establish that all inoculation effects are absent; precise pooled efficacy claims remain withheld pending outcome-specific extraction review [@ageint182].
title: Psychological Inoculation Against Misinformation: Corrected and Contested Meta-Analysis

raw: 39.3 Prebunking Interventions Based on Inoculation Theory (Harvard Kennedy School)[^183]
teaching_note: A game-based intervention, a short video, and a transparent source-checking lesson differ in content, participation, comparator, and outcome. Active inoculation means contributing to refutation, not simply using a digital game; medium alone is an inadequate classification rule. This curriculum uses supplied benign examples and explanation, not practice producing influence campaigns, and does not infer real-world behavioral protection from a post-task rating change [@ageint183; @ageint182].
title: Prebunking Interventions Based on Inoculation Theory (Harvard Kennedy School)

raw: 39.4 Cambridge/Jigsaw YouTube Field Study: 5.4 Million Users, 7 Experiments[^152]
teaching_note: The primary article distinguishes six online studies from study 7 on YouTube; the field study is not an additional eighth experiment. Its denominator ledger is: about 5.4 million shown ads; 967,347 watched at least 30 seconds; 22,632 answered a test item (11,432 treatment, 11,200 control) within 24 hours. Reach and substantial views are not the analyzed outcome sample, and the Cambridge news account describes the same research rather than an independent replication. The article's stated six-study total conflicts with its listed component counts, so no exact combined online-study total is adopted here [@ageint152; @scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation].
title: Cambridge/Jigsaw: Six Online Studies and a Seventh YouTube Field Study

raw: 39.4.1 Inoculation Effect: Measured Improvement in Manipulation Recognition[^152]
teaching_note: Study 7 tested one technique-recognition item per respondent, not observed sharing, factual accuracy across topics, or durable immunity. The overall field effect was h = 0.09, below the preregistered smallest effect of interest h = 0.10; statistical significance is not the same as reaching the prespecified practical target. Without neutral field items, that field test cannot establish the same recognition-versus-false-alarm discernment measured in the online studies, and the within-24-hour assessment does not establish long-term retention [@scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation].
title: Measured Manipulation Recognition: Outcome and Follow-Up Limits

raw: 39.4.2 Source-Agnostic Design: Effective Across Political Affiliations[^152]
teaching_note: The online studies reported no consistently significant treatment-by-covariate interactions, including ideology; this is not an equivalence test proving identical effects in every affiliation or population. Source-agnostic technique examples do not eliminate language, cultural, recruitment, and item-design constraints. Use nonpolitical, fictional items here and do not profile or target learners by politics, inferred susceptibility, or identity [@scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation].
title: Source-Agnostic Design and Measured Moderation Limits

raw: 39.4.3 Scaling at $0.05 Per View; Campaign Applications[^152]
teaching_note: The approximately $0.05 figure is cost per 30-second video view in that campaign, not cost per corrected belief, prevented share, lasting benefit, or successful learner. A large impression count cannot repair a small or narrowly measured effect. The educational design here is transparent, opt-in, accessible, and debriefed, with an equivalent nonparticipatory worksheet; it is not an audience-targeting or covert persuasion campaign [@scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation].
title: Study-Specific Cost per View: What Scaling Does Not Establish

teaching_note: An author's professional affiliation or an abstract's introductory summary is not evidence of intervention magnitude, durability, or independent replication. Extract the actual population, comparison, outcome, and time point before using a cited account as empirical support; if these are unavailable, retain it as conceptual context. Inoculation remains a psychological metaphor here, not a medical treatment or a basis for judging an individual's mental health [@ageint184].
title: Psychological Inoculation (JNNP, van der Linden 2023)

teaching_note: A clinical-journal venue does not convert a discussion of misinformation education into clinical evidence or a prescription. Separate an account of an approach from the underlying experiments and from recommendations about public communication. No learner health disclosure, diagnosis, or medical decision is part of this lesson; unsupported generalizations about resistance remain unknown [@ageint185].
title: "Inoculation" to Resist Misinformation (JAMA, 2024)

raw: 39.7 Psychological Inoculation Against Misinformation: Current Evidence and Boundary Conditions (ANNALS, 2022)[^186]
teaching_note: Recognition of a taught technique, transfer to an untaught technique, retention over time, and changed behavior are separate claims requiring separate measurements. A fall in ratings of both misleading and accurate items can reflect generalized distrust rather than better discrimination. A review helps identify these boundary questions but cannot substitute for a particular study's comparator, item set, response-bias analysis, and follow-up [@ageint186].
title: Psychological Inoculation Against Misinformation: Evidence and Boundary Conditions

raw: 39.8 NATO STRATCOM COE: Inoculation Theory and Misinformation (PDF)[^187]
teaching_note: An institutional report supplies a strategic-communication perspective, not a blanket endorsement by NATO or proof that a classroom technique works. Distinguish its recommendations from measured study outcomes and preserve any study-specific population limits. Neither an institutional label nor an information-disorder category establishes a speaker's intent or authorizes intervention against a real audience [@ageint187].
title: NATO STRATCOM COE: Inoculation Theory and Misinformation

teaching_note: **Completed synthetic lesson and counterexample.** An opt-in worksheet explains false dichotomy using the fictional claim 'The museum must open every room or close forever'; supplied option C, opening one wing, refutes the forced choice. Its matched neutral item states 'The museum may open one wing while repairs continue'; a truthful emotional item, 'We are delighted the east entrance reopened', and an ordinary disagreement are not automatically coded manipulative. In a wholly fictional eight-item answer record (four technique items, four neutral), pre-lesson hits = 2/4 and false alarms = 1/4; post-lesson hits = 3/4 and false alarms = 3/4, so hit-minus-false-alarm separation falls from 0.25 to 0 despite more hits. Decision: reject the inflated 'recognition improved, therefore resilience improved' summary, revise the lesson to protect neutral judgments, and stop on distress or personal accusations. A supplied later card reports only two of three invited fictional records returned at one week: retention and generalization remain unresolved, and none of these invented numbers validates an intervention [@ageint151].
title: A Practical Guide to Prebunking (Cambridge/Jigsaw/BBC)

raw: 39.10 Critical Thinking Training vs. Misinformation: Systematic Review (Nature Comms, 2025)[^181]
teaching_note: The primary record is Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, published online 9 December 2025, volume 13/article 53 (2026), not Nature Communications. It selected 17 studies, only seven rigorously meeting eligibility criteria, mainly involving higher-education participants; heterogeneous interventions and measures prevented a clear overall effectiveness verdict. Contrast explicit critical-thinking instruction and source checking with technique-focused prebunking, without assuming either dominates for every outcome or that reported confidence is demonstrated critical-thinking skill [@ageint181].
title: Critical-Thinking Training Review: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, 2025/2026

raw: 39.11 Operationalizing Prebunking in AGEINT: Transparent Resilience Education and Review
teaching_note: An educational decision needs separate judgments of factual support, technique cue, intent (usually unknown), and proportionate response. Compare the fictional lesson with a supplied-source-checking alternative; report all item denominators, neutral-item errors, missing follow-up, and accessibility constraints rather than only a favorable hit count. Participation must be transparent and optional with debrief and a no-penalty alternative; stop if the exercise becomes audience profiling, belief steering, or reputational accusation. The inherited influence-policy citations provide governance context, not empirical validation of this lesson [@ageint151; @sec:analytic-workflow].
title: Operationalizing Prebunking in AGEINT: Transparent Resilience Education and Review
